_doc: Monitoring alert template for PARK Token deployments. Operators MUST instantiate this per chain (BSC, Arbitrum, future) before any production deploy. Hook into Tenderly Alerts, Forta agents, OpenZeppelin Defender Sentinels, or in-house infra. CertiK pre-audit H-03 + M-06; audit-2026-05-10 CR-02/CR-03/H-03/M-03 (event signature fixes + bytes32 role hashes + UPGRADER grant alert + pre-execute updateDelay detector + CallExecuted reconciliation).

_substitution_keys.${PAGER_EMAIL}: operator email or PagerDuty webhook URL

_role_hashes._doc: OZ canonical role hashes — substitute literals into provider rules; do NOT use symbolic names (audit CR-02). Each is keccak256(role-name).

_function_selectors._doc: Used by pre-execute Timelock proposal decoders. selector = keccak256(signature)[0:4].

alerts.rationale: Reducing minDelay below 6h shortens the operator's reaction window before any subsequent upgrade. Reject any value below the documented production policy. POST-EXECUTE backstop — primary detection is TIMELOCK-UPDATEDELAY-PRE-EXECUTE below.

trigger.event: CallScheduled(bytes32 id, uint256 index, address target, uint256 value, bytes data, bytes32 predecessor, uint256 delay)

alerts.rationale: Pre-execute detector for Timelock self-calls invoking updateDelay(uint256). Catches a delay-reduction proposal at SCHEDULE time, before the delay window elapses — operator can call cancel(opId) within getMinDelay() seconds. Audit CR-03.

trigger.event: RoleGranted(bytes32 role, address account, address sender)

alerts.rationale: TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE granted to anything other than the Timelock contract itself breaks the role-isolation invariant and lets the new holder grant UPGRADER_ROLE arbitrarily. Mega-review M-3.

trigger.event: RoleGranted(bytes32 role, address account, address sender)

alerts.rationale: UPGRADER_ROLE granted to anything other than the Timelock contract bypasses the entire timelock-mediated upgrade protection — the new holder can immediately call upgradeToAndCall on the proxy. Audit CR-02 (closes the blind spot — symmetric coverage with TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE grant alert).

trigger.event: RoleRevoked(bytes32 role, address account, address sender)

alerts.rationale: Revoking UPGRADER_ROLE from the Timelock breaks all subsequent upgrades until re-grant via the Timelock itself (chicken-and-egg recovery window of getMinDelay()). Mega-review L-4 / UPGRADE-HAZARDS H-8.

Scheduling a transfer to address(0) is the OZ DefaultAdminRules signal for renouncing DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE permanently. After acceptSchedule elapses + acceptDefaultAdminTransfer call, mint/setContractURI/RESCUER administration become impossible forever. CertiK H-06 / mega-review M-4.
Implementation slot changed. Operator must verify the new impl matches the published audit artefact + run scripts/repro.sh against the new commit. Trigger explorer mark-as-proxy refresh.

trigger.event: CallScheduled(bytes32 id, uint256 index, address target, uint256 value, bytes data, bytes32 predecessor, uint256 delay)

alerts.rationale: Visibility on every governance proposal entering the queue. Cross-check target/data against expected upgrade calldata; abnormal targets trigger investigation. Pre-execute decoders (TIMELOCK-UPDATEDELAY-PRE-EXECUTE above) handle CRITICAL cases inline.

trigger.event: CallExecuted(bytes32 id, uint256 index, address target, uint256 value, bytes data)

alerts.rationale: Closes out the schedule->execute lifecycle. Operator dashboard correlates id with prior CallScheduled to confirm zero-drift. Audit M-03 (closes the schedule/execute reconciliation gap).
A scheduled operation was cancelled before execute(). Could be benign (operator change of mind) or hostile (cancellation of a legitimate upgrade by a compromised CANCELLER). Investigate per case.

trigger.event: Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value)

alerts.rationale: Token mint after initial deployment. Should only happen after a holder burn + admin re-mint up to cap. Routine mints during distribution are expected; unexpected mints indicate compromised DEFAULT_ADMIN.

trigger.event: RescuedERC20(address indexed token, address indexed to, uint256 amount, address indexed operator)

alerts.rationale: ERC-20 rescue invoked. Confirm against operator-side ticket; any rescue without a ticket = potential RESCUER key compromise. Audit H-03: split from combined rule + corrected to 4-arg signature including 'operator' (matches contracts/ParkToken.sol emission).

trigger.event: RescuedETH(address indexed to, uint256 amount, address indexed operator)

alerts.rationale: ETH rescue invoked. Confirm against operator-side ticket. Audit H-03: split from combined rule + corrected to 3-arg signature including 'operator' (matches contracts/ParkToken.sol emission).
Metadata URI swap (token-metadata.json content). Cross-check the new URI resolves to a sane document.

tenderly.alertConfigPath: https://dashboard.tenderly.co/alerts -> New rule -> Event filter; paste address + event signature + filter expression
tenderly.notes: Free tier supports basic event-based alerts; paid for filter expressions on event arg values and pre-execute calldata decoders.

openZeppelinDefender.notes: Conditions DSL covers role hash + address comparisons + ABI-decoded function args. Free tier sufficient for this 13-alert set.

forta.alertConfigPath: Custom Forta agent — write a TS/JS handler matching the event sigs above
forta.notes: Higher-effort; Forta excels at multi-tx pattern detection rather than single-event alerts. Pre-execute Timelock decoders are easiest in Forta.

_install_test_required: Before relying on these rules in production, the operator MUST test-fire each alert in the chosen provider — fork the chain or replay a known-matching tx and confirm the alert delivers. Audit CR-02 explicitly requires this validation step.
